productGuide.title: Getting Started
productGuide.intro: Build, test, understand and integrate your Tree.
productGuide.quick: Quick Start · your real setup progress

overview.title: Understand AgentTree
paragraphs: A Tree is a reusable team of AI Agents with one Root, Managers and their Specialists. Your application sends a task to the Tree; AgentTree coordinates the internal work.

Root owns the overall task, decides whether to answer directly or delegate, performs final review of delegated work and synthesizes the answer. Managers divide and review their part. Specialists do focused work.
Start small: one Root, one Manager and one Specialist are enough to learn the delegated workflow. Some tasks legitimately take Root’s direct response path.

credentials.title: Prepare Secret, then Provider
paragraphs: For a Provider that needs a credential, open Secrets → Add Secret. Give it a recognizable name, choose the supported type and save the credential. Stored values are encrypted and shown masked.

Open Providers → connect a Provider. Select the saved Secret, configure the service and test it. Local Ollama or a credential-free compatible service may not need a Secret; use the selected Provider’s actual fields.

Discover and verify Models. Connection success alone does not qualify every Model. Choose a Model that Studio has verified as usable; unavailable or temporarily failed Models need diagnosis or later retry.

build.title: Create and configure a Tree
paragraphs: Choose Create Tree → Visual Builder for direct Canvas construction, or Guided Wizard for step-by-step setup. Both create the same Tree. Templates → Use Template opens the existing Visual Builder draft; cancellation before Save creates no Tree.

Keep exactly one Root. Connect Root → Manager and Manager → Specialist. Click an Agent to inspect it, then Edit to configure its instructions, capabilities, Provider and Model. Save persists a new configuration version.

Capability describes suitable work, such as research or evidence-review. Routing matches capabilities, not Agent names. Use clear, specific labels and give Managers and Specialists responsibilities that align.

resources.title: Tools, MCP and readiness
paragraphs: Tools let an Agent access services, data or produce supported outputs. Basic text-only Trees do not require a Tool. Add one only when the task needs an external action. Some Templates declare required Tool slots.

MCP connects compatible external Tool servers through supported stdio or Streamable HTTP transports. Configure/test/discover the actual resource in Tools, then bind it to an Agent. MCP is a Tool integration, not communication with another AgentTree system.

The Builder displays shared resources once while keeping independent Agent bindings. Readiness comes from backend validation: resolve missing Models, invalid hierarchy, unavailable resources or required setup before testing.

test.title: Test in Playground
paragraphs: Select a Ready Tree explicitly, open Playground, enter realistic test input and choose Run Tree. Each submission creates an independent real Execution with a new Run ID; previous messages are not conversation memory.

Watch real Agent activity, then inspect Result, Execution Trace and Artifacts. Cancel requests a cooperative stop; wait for confirmed Cancelled. Run Again submits a new Execution. Return to Builder to fix configuration and save before the next test.

Executions keeps historical work. Search by Run ID or Tree name, combine status/Tree/local date-time filters, and open the same persisted Execution. Browser reload restores saved results/events; interrupted active work does not resume after a backend process restart.

review.title: Manager Review → Root Final Review
paragraphs: Manager checks each Specialist result against its subtask objective. PASS accepts that work. REVISE requests Specialist changes and another review within the configured Manager revision limit. FAIL rejects it.

After Manager results return, Root reviews the combined work against the overall task. Root PASS allows final synthesis. Root REVISE returns feedback to Managers to review previous work again; Specialists rerun only when Manager review requests a revision.

Root and Manager revision budgets are separately bounded. A failed review or exhausted budget can prevent success. Human-readable Trace presents only recorded activity; technical details retain all events and safe payloads. Trace is runtime evidence, not hidden AI reasoning.

outputs.title: Final Result and Artifacts
paragraphs: Final Result is the primary answer to the task. It may be text, JSON or structured output according to the saved Tree settings. Inspect its actual status: a partial result is not complete approval.

Artifacts are additional outputs preserved separately: for example text, a generated file or a patch produced through supported runtime/Tools. Open Preview for supported text or download available bytes. Artifacts are not Agents, Executions or Trace.
A file intent is not an applied change. AgentTree does not automatically edit your workspace. Review the content and decide how your own application should use it.

api.title: Call a Tree from your application
paragraphs: Playground tests a Tree inside Studio. Public API uses the same Tree/runtime from your application; Playground is not required for external use. Create a personal key in Account → API Keys, store it server-side, then choose a Ready Tree and open Connect.

API Key authenticates who calls; Tree ID selects which workflow; input is the work to do. Current account permissions and Tree grants apply on every request. An API Key does not bind to one arbitrary Tree or provide Provider credentials.

Public input is nonempty text, at most 65,536 characters. Serialize structured source data into text. V1 metadata accepts client_request_id only; V2 accepts bounded metadata and optional timeout_seconds. Do not send Agent configuration, endpoints or Provider credentials.

versions.title: V1 / V2 and starter code
paragraphs: V1 is synchronous: POST /api/v1/trees/{TREE_ID}/invoke waits, then returns run_id, status and output.content. Use it for simple request-response work. Runtime failure can return HTTP 200 with status failed; check the body as well as HTTP status.

V2 is recommended for longer tasks: POST /api/v2/runs returns HTTP 202 and run_id. Poll /api/v2/runs/{RUN_ID}; when terminal, GET /result for final_output, final_status and Artifact refs. Before terminal, result returns 409. Status, events, SSE, cancel and artifacts use the same Run ID.

The examples below use a placeholder TREE_ID. Choose your Tree explicitly and use Connect for code with its actual ID and deployment-aware Base URL. Python needs requests; JavaScript runs server-side in Node.js with native fetch, not in browser code. Set AGENTTREE_API_KEY securely in the environment.

integrations.title: Direct API, Webhook and Result Destination
paragraphs: Direct API is the normal path when your application submits work and retrieves the result. Incoming Webhook is optional: an external event source pushes text input to a configured authenticated ingress, which starts a real Execution.

Result Destination goes in the opposite direction: AgentTree sends completed output to a configured external URL. It is separate from incoming Webhook authentication and from API response retrieval. Configure these in the selected Tree’s existing Connect page.

First build and test a small workflow, inspect its reviews and outputs, then connect it to your application. Generic integration capabilities are available; the Wazuh, Network and Software Development case studies are planned, not completed.
